Hi Anita / team —

Attached is a one-page draft dataflow (redwood-dataflow-brightwell.pdf). Highlights:
- Ingest: customer request arrives at public API (TLS). Plaintext payload is held briefly in an in-memory buffer and forwarded to the inference runtime.
- Tokenization: customers may opt into tokenization/pseudonymization at client side or via our proxy; default hosted flow does not tokenize by default. We call out an optional Customer-Side Tokenization pattern.
- KV cache: KV caches are encrypted at rest; cache entries may contain transient context (<=24h default) and are scoped per-customer.
- KMS custody: Customer-managed KMS is supported for key material used to encrypt persisted telemetry; otherwise Redwood-managed keys are used for transient caches.
- Subprocessors: inference runtime (managed cluster), telemetry pipeline (logging vendor), and metrics/usage analytics (analytics vendor).

I flagged 3 areas where BrightWell may want tighter controls:
1) Request-level tokenization (client-side) to avoid plaintext in transit and caches.
2) KMS bring-your-own-key for telemetry exports.
3) Additional contractual restriction on analytics subprocessors to limit retention.

I'll attach the PDF here and will update it after Marissa adds the evidence links.

Attachments: redwood-dataflow-brightwell.pdf

Best,
Kimberly

Anita / Samir —

Thanks for the patience; attached are: 1) a populated SSQ (BrightWell_Security_Questionnaire_v1.xlsx), 2) the dataflow PDF (redwood-dataflow-brightwell.pdf), and 3) a DPA annex draft (dpa-annex-draft.docx) that incorporates BYOK and a subprocessor retention clause as discussed.

Short summary of answers and commitments:
- PII handling: plaintext is not stored persistently by default; transient in-memory buffers and encrypted caches are the primary runtime exposures. Customer-side tokenization is strongly recommended for regulated PII.
- Subprocessor custody: Aditya included an appendix listing subprocessors and indicating whether they handle plaintext (inference runtime nodes occasionally during live inference), derived tokens only (analytics), or metadata/metrics only.
- Logs & exports: we can provide exportable audit logs for access to PII, redacted on request; raw request payload exports require a legal process and are subject to access controls. We'll provide a summary export for procurement review.
- Timeline: we can deliver the evidence bundle + signed DPA annex within 5 business days if legal review does not require material redlines.

Next steps: please confirm if Samir wants a walkthrough; we can set up a 45-minute working session Thursday or Friday. If procurement needs DocuSign, I've added the annex to the related_links for prefill.

Regards,
Lauren

Anita — quick legal clarity on the three asks from Lauren's package: 

1) Subprocessor retention clause: Redwood is willing to negotiate a retention cap for analytics-derived outputs; however, operationally we need an exception for aggregated metrics required for SLA and billing reconciliations. Proposed compromise: 30-day retention for per-customer derived outputs, 365-day retention for aggregated metrics tied to billing and platform health, with contractual protections limiting use.

2) Legal hold / raw payload export: We can produce raw request payloads if compelled or via an approved legal disclosure request. Approval requires a narrow set of approvers (Product Security + Legal Director); expected turnaround for a scoped export is 3–7 business days, and we will provide a chain-of-custody artifact (signed access log + export manifest). We prefer to avoid ad-hoc raw exports without a legal basis; however, for procurement/sample audits we can produce redacted egress logs without the full legal process.

3) One-off export of egress logs: Possible — we can provide a redacted sample set for audit purposes within 48–72 hours provided the scope is narrow (time window and account ids). No raw payloads in the sample.

I'll work with Marissa to add these notes into the DPA annex and the SSQ evidence column.

Rishi
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
